name: Edomites
summary: The descendants of Esau, Jacob's twin brother, who lived in the red mountains of Seir south of the Dead Sea. The twins' rivalry carried on between their nations for more than a thousand years, from Edom refusing Israel passage to Edom cheering Jerusalem's fall. It ended with an Idumean dynasty, the Herods, ruling Judea when Jesus was born.
name_meaning: Edom means 'red' — from the red pottage for which Esau sold his birthright, from his ruddy appearance at birth, and fittingly from the red sandstone of their mountains.

origin.account: Rebekah bore twins to Isaac; the first came out red and hairy and was named Esau. Coming in faint from the field, Esau sold his birthright to Jacob for red lentil pottage, 'therefore was his name called Edom.' Esau married Canaanite and Ishmaelite wives and moved to Mount Seir, where his sons became the 'dukes' of Edom.

lineage.notes: Esau's wives were Adah daughter of Elon the Hittite, Aholibamah daughter of Anah the Hivite, and Bashemath (Mahalath) daughter of Ishmael. So Edom mixed Abrahamic, Canaanite, Ishmaelite and Horite blood: Esau's line intermarried with the Horites of Seir, including Timna, mother of Amalek. Genesis 36 lists Edom's dukes and eight kings who 'reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Israel.'

homeland.region: Edom / Mount Seir — south and south-east of the Dead Sea
homeland.description: A rugged highland of red sandstone and granite running from the Zered brook south to the Gulf of Aqaba, on both sides of the Arabah rift. Rich in copper (Faynan) and on the King's Highway trade route. Its cities were built on rock heights — 'thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock'. After the 6th century BC Edomites moved into the southern Judean hills, which Greeks and Romans called Idumea.
homeland.modern_location: Southern Jordan (Tafilah, Ma'an, Aqaba governorates) and, for later Idumea, the Negev and southern Hebron hills in Israel and the West Bank.

timeline.event: Jacob and Esau struggle in the womb: 'two nations are in thy womb… the elder shall serve the younger.'
Esau loses the birthright and the blessing; he is told he will live by the sword and one day break Jacob's yoke. The brothers are later reconciled.
Esau's children destroy the Horites and take Seir.
Edom refuses Israel passage on the King's Highway; Israel goes around. Moses commands, 'Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother.'
Doeg the Edomite massacres the priests of Nob for Saul. David later places garrisons throughout Edom; Hadad, an Edomite prince, escapes to Egypt and later troubles Solomon.
Edom revolts under Jehoram of Judah and makes its own king, fulfilling Isaac's word.
Amaziah of Judah kills ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt and takes Sela.
When Babylon destroys Jerusalem, Edom rejoices, blocks the escape routes and hands over survivors — the sin condemned by Obadiah and Psalm 137.
Arab tribes and then the Nabataeans occupy Edom proper; Edomites settle southern Judah (Idumea).
The Hasmonean ruler John Hyrcanus conquers Idumea and requires the Idumeans to be circumcised and keep the Jewish law (Josephus).
Herod the Great, of Idumean descent, rules Judea under Rome; he seeks to kill the infant Jesus.

religion.practices: The Bible names Edom's gods only in passing; Amaziah brought back 'the gods of the children of Seir' and worshipped them. Inscriptions and personal names show the chief Edomite god was Qos. Herod's family, and Idumea after Hyrcanus, were outwardly Jewish.

importance: Edom embodies the story of two brothers. God chose Jacob over the older Esau before they were born, which Paul uses to show that election rests on God's mercy, not works. Yet Israel was told not to hate Edom 'for he is thy brother'. When Edom turned that brotherhood into betrayal at Jerusalem's fall, a whole prophetic book (Obadiah) was given against it. In the New Testament an Idumean king kills the children of Bethlehem, and Hebrews warns believers not to be like 'profane' Esau, who sold his birthright for one meal.

impact.how: His fear of Esau and their reconciliation shaped his return to Canaan; at Peniel, before meeting Esau, he became 'Israel'.
Edom's refusal lengthened the journey and the people 'was much discouraged because of the way'.
Doeg the Edomite killed eighty-five priests.
Edom cut off fleeing Judeans in 586 BC.
Herod the Idumean ordered their massacre.
Esau is the New Testament example of trading lasting blessing for immediate appetite.

key_verses.text: And the LORD said unto her, Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels; and the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.
Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.
Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother: thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian; because thou wast a stranger in his land.
For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.

I have loved you, saith the LORD. Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the LORD: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.

fate.summary: Edom proper was lost to Arab tribes and the Nabataeans after the 6th century BC. The Edomites who moved into southern Judah were forcibly joined to the Jewish nation by John Hyrcanus. Idumean soldiers fought in the Jewish revolt against Rome (Josephus, Jewish War 4). After the destruction of Jerusalem in AD 70 the Idumeans disappear from history. Obadiah had said: 'there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau.'

today.summary: No people today are identified as Edomites. Their land is southern Jordan, home to Petra and the copper valley of Faynan. In later Jewish writing 'Edom' became a code name for Rome and then for Christendom, so the name lived on as a symbol rather than a nation.
today.descendants: Merged into the Jewish people (after Hyrcanus) and into the Arab populations of southern Jordan and the Negev.
today.modern_legacy: Excavations at Buseira (Bozrah), Tawilan, Umm el-Biyara and Faynan have filled in Edom's Iron Age history; the copper mines at Khirbat en-Nahas are among the largest of the ancient Near East.

archaeology.name: Khirbat en-Nahas copper works
archaeology.discovered: Excavated 2002 onward by Thomas Levy and Mohammad Najjar
archaeology.significance: Large-scale industrial copper production early in the Iron Age. It challenged the view that Edom only became organised in the 8th century BC.

archaeology.name: Buseira (Bozrah) excavations
archaeology.significance: Palace and temple complex of Edom's capital.

archaeology.name: Horvat Qitmit shrine
archaeology.significance: Edomite shrine inside Judah's former territory, with Qos inscriptions — evidence of Edom's move west.

archaeology.name: Papyrus Anastasi VI
archaeology.significance: Egyptian border official lets 'the Shasu tribes of Edom' water their flocks in the Delta — an early outside mention of Edom.
